item.title: College basketball picks for Tuesday: Duke vs. Illinois, Michigan State vs. Tennessee and more best bets
item.description: College basketball best bets for Nov. 17: Duke -7.5 vs. Illinois, Hofstra +11.5, Notre Dame +15.5, Michigan State -2.5 and the under in Knoxville.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday is the first college basketball card of the season that feels like it matters. Two top-10 teams meet in Durham, Michigan State brings its Duke-beating defense into Knoxville to battle Tennessee, and the undercard is full of spots where the betting market has guessed wrong.

I’ve got four plays, starting at 4:30 p.m. and running later into the night. Some of them back the favorite, and some take the points. All of them come down to the same idea: trust what the numbers say, not the names on the front of the jerseys.

4:30 p.m. ET, Gainesville

Fifteen and a half points is a lot to give a team that shoots like Notre Dame.

The Irish rank first in the country in three-point percentage at 47.8%, and they’re shooting 50.4% from the field overall. Teams that shoot that well from deep don’t fall behind by 16 very often. Even when they’re losing, a couple of late threes keeps the backdoor wide open.

Notre Dame has also been one of the most reliable bets in the sport after a cover, going 6-0-1 against the spread in its last seven games following an ATS win. The Irish are coming in with five days of rest, compared with three for Florida.

The concern is the glass, where Florida ranks 36th in rebounding and Notre Dame ranks 180th. If the Gators control the boards, this could get away from the Irish. But a team that shoots this well doesn’t need many possessions to cover a 15.5-point spread.

The pick: Notre Dame +15.5

7 p.m. ET, Cameron Indoor Stadium, ESPN

Everyone loves Illinois this week, and I understand why. The Illini have the most efficient offense in the country. They’ve made 75% of their two-point attempts and topped 108 points three times. Andrej Stojakovic is averaging 22.3 points per game on 61.8% shooting.

But Illinois is walking into Cameron Indoor, and Duke is still upset about Michigan State.

Duke ranks second nationally in overall efficiency and third on both offense and defense. Opponents are averaging 57 points per game against the Blue Devils, and three of their four opponents have scored 52 or fewer. Duke is 3-0 at home and 3-1 against the spread.

Illinois’ defense is the weak spot. The Illini allow 71.3 points per game and just gave up 86 to Sam Houston. They’re 0-1 on the road, having lost 84-78 at Texas Tech, and they’ll be without forward David Mirkovic, who’s out after an appendectomy.

The public sees the best offense in America getting 7.5 points. I see an elite defense at home, with a week to think about its only loss.

The pick: Duke -7.5 (-108)

OVER/UNDER BETTING EXPLAINED: HOW TOTALS BETS WORK IN THE NFL, NBA AND MLB

9 p.m. ET, Knoxville

This is the matchup I’m playing twice, because both bets rely on the same weakness.

WHAT IS A TEASER BET? HOW TEASERS WORK IN FOOTBALL AND BASKETBALL BETTING

Tennessee is 3-0, but those wins came against the 336th-ranked schedule in the country. The Vols are shooting under 31% from three. Their 302nd ranking in offensive block percentage means opponents are swatting their shots at the rim, too. Now they face a Michigan State defense that ranks fifth in adjusted efficiency and ninth in block percentage.

Michigan State is also built to win the possession battle. The Spartans rank fifth in offensive rebounding percentage, and Tennessee ranks 258th in defensive rebounding. That’s a lot of second chances for Michigan State. Jeremy Fears Jr. is the best player on the floor, and the Spartans already proved they can win a big road-style game by beating Duke.

The total comes down to style, not star power. Tennessee’s defense is legitimate, ranking 29th in adjusted efficiency and allowing 61.3 points per game. Michigan State gives up 66.3. Two physical, deliberate teams with one offense that can’t hit a three is a recipe for a game in the 130s.

The picks: Michigan State -2.5 and under 149.5 (-110)

Odds subject to change.

item.title: Pizza Hut co-founder dies at 95 as iconic chain returns to its roots nearly 70 years after $600 start
item.description: From a $600 loan to a $300 million PepsiCo sale, Dan Carney helped build Pizza Hut into the world's largest pizza chain, now embracing its nostalgic past.
item.content:encoded:
The death of Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney at the age of 95 marks the end of an era for one of America's most recognizable restaurant chains — a brand that is now turning to its past to attract a new generation of customers.

What began as a small pizza restaurant in Wichita, Kansas, in 1958 grew into a global empire known for its distinctive red roofs, family dining rooms and nostalgic atmosphere.

Carney and his younger brother, Frank, borrowed $600 from their mother, Mary, and purchased secondhand equipment to open their first Pizza Hut, according to the Kansas Historical Society.

FIREHOUSE SUBS CO-FOUNDER DIES AFTER BUILDING BELOVED AMERICAN SANDWICH CHAIN WITH BROTHER

The restaurant quickly caught on, and the brothers opened their first franchised location in Topeka, Kansas, the following year.

By 1971, Pizza Hut had become the world's largest pizza restaurant chain in both sales and number of locations, according to the company's website.

Six years later, the brothers sold Pizza Hut to PepsiCo for approximately $300 million.

As the chain expanded, it developed a recognizable identity, including Pizza Pete, a mustachioed cartoon mascot sporting a checkered neckerchief, apron and hat.

AMERICA'S BEST-TASTING PIZZA CHAIN IS AN OLD-SCHOOL FAVORITE, SURVEY FINDS

The character was created by Ed Pointer, an illustrator and fraternity brother of Dan Carney, according to Wichita State University's Pizza Hut Museum.

Pete appeared on advertisements, drinking cups, bags and restaurant signs, becoming one of the company's earliest recognizable symbols.

RESTAURANTS BRING BACK OLD-SCHOOL HOSPITALITY AS NOSTALGIA TAKES HOLD ACROSS AMERICA

Pizza Hut also became a fixture of American family dining, with its signature red-roof restaurants, vinyl booths, stained-glass-style lamps and red plastic drinking cups.

For generations of Americans, a trip to Pizza Hut meant more than grabbing a slice. It was a destination for birthday parties, family dinners and celebrations.

But as dining habits changed, the chain increasingly shifted toward delivery and carryout, leaving many of its traditional sit-down restaurants behind.

Nearly seven decades after its founding, some Pizza Hut franchisees are betting that the chain's past could help shape its future.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The Pizza Hut Classic concept, which began around 2017, brings back the familiar atmosphere of the 1980s and 1990s, complete with checkerboard tablecloths, Tiffany-style lamps and other vintage touches.

The throwback restaurants have become a hit with customers, some traveling hours to relive childhood memories.

Tim Sparks, president of Wichita, Kansas-based Daland Corp., which operates dozens of dine-in Pizza Hut restaurants, previously told Fox News Digital that the nostalgic atmosphere has struck a chord with diners.

In Homosassa Springs, Florida, dine-in sales more than doubled after a restaurant was converted to the classic format, FOX 13 Tampa Bay reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Sparks said the restaurants also appear to encourage something increasingly rare in modern dining: customers putting down their phones and enjoying conversations.

Today, the original 1958 Pizza Hut building stands on the campus of Wichita State University, where it serves as a museum celebrating the chain's history.

The building was relocated to the university in 1986 and became a museum featuring memorabilia and artifacts from the company's early years.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Visitors can even pose for photographs with a likeness of Pizza Pete, whose image remains a permanent fixture at the museum.

It's a reminder of how a modest family investment helped create one of America's most recognizable restaurant brands.

item.title: Dan Campbell won't stop players from celebrating even after star Aidan Hutchinson was injured celebrating
item.description: Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL after a sack of Drake Maye, and Dan Campbell refuses to curb Lions celebrations, saying the NFL game is built off of emotion.
item.content:encoded:
After Aidan Hutchinson tore the ACL in his right knee, which means he's done playing the remainder of the NFL season, the logical question around the league is whether coaches have to crack down on players celebrating big plays because that's exactly how the Detroit Lions defensive end got injured.

Well, Lions coach Dan Campbell isn't going there.

Campbell was asked Tuesday on his weekly appearance on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit if he needs to have a discussion with his players about not celebrating or toning down celebrations.

LIONS STAR HURT CELEBRATING SACK OF PATRIOTS' DRAKE MAY AS BOTH INJURED ON POSSIBLE SEASON-ALTERING PLAY

"No, I don’t believe that," Campbell said. "I think what happened speaks for itself. We’re not talking to eight-year-olds here."

Campbell played in the NFL. He played 11 seasons for four teams and he shared his experience with celebrations.

"I remember one time I made a big play and I freaking pumped my arm up and I’m pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn’t tell anybody," Campbell said. "I was just excited. I just pumped my arm.

"So if you say, 'Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic,' man, this game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you gotta keep your head -- then you’re really becoming something you’re not."

Hutchinson blew out his right knee after he sacked New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye during the Lions' game against the Patriots in Munich. The injury happened after the sack when Hutchinson leaped into the air and his knee buckled when he landed.

"Look, it was one of those things. I hate it, I know he hates it," Campbell said. "But I mean, the number of moves that I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral balances, I’m just like, 'It was one of those things, man.'

"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let’s be smart, but no, I’m not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore.'"

NFL RESCINDS JAMESON WILLIAMS' SMOKING CELEBRATION FINE AFTER HE ARGUES 'MARIJUANA IS LEGAL'

Obviously, this is one man's opinion.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

There is no telling what will happen around the NFL on Wednesday when most teams gather to begin preparations for Sunday's games.

Some coaches may ignore the Hutchinson injury and move along. Some may caution their players to be more careful during celebrations.

The really interesting thing is whether some NFL coach decides getting injured during a celebration is the most preventable injury ever and tells his players to keep their feet planted when they celebrate.

Or if some coach decides his players must cut out celebrations altogether – even if Dan Campbell is fine with them.

item.title: LAPD warns parents about student safety, says '3rd party organizers' recruit kids for anti-ICE walkouts
item.description: Thousands of Los Angeles students walked out over ICE enforcement as LAPD says outside organizers recruited kids through social media to protest.
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of Los Angeles high school students walked out of class Monday to protest federal immigration enforcement, with demonstrators gathering at City Hall, blocking downtown streets and damaging vehicles, according to police.

Hundreds of students gathered outside Los Angeles City Hall before marching through downtown, while others rallied at Huntington Park City Hall. Organizers called for an end to ICE operations and demanded that LAUSD fund "dream centers" on every campus to provide immigration information, mental health support and basic necessities, the Los Angeles Times reported.

LAPD Capt. Kelly Muniz told Fox News Digital that outside organizers recruited students through social media and other channels. She said LAUSD and school police did not organize or endorse the demonstrations.

"LAUSD did not condone this or facilitate this," Muniz said. "LA school police, same thing. These are third-party organizers that are getting kids through social media and other avenues to join these things."

ANTI-ICE WALKOUT EXPOSES HOW SCHOOL DISTRICT 'FAILED' PARENTS, RISKED STUDENT SAFETY: 'BROKEN MY TRUST'

"Now you're leaving the safety of your children in the hands of people that, as we can see here, really didn't take measures to secure their safety," she continued.

Responding to demands to end ICE operations, the Department of Homeland Security told Fox News Digital that federal enforcement would continue.

"Make no mistake: ICE is not going anywhere, and we will continue to target the worst of the worst in sanctuary cities who refuse to jail criminal illegal aliens," a DHS spokesperson said. "To be clear: ICE does not target schools. This is just another false narrative to try and demonize our brave ICE law enforcement who are facing a 1,600% increase in assaults against them and an 8,000% increase in death threats."

EXCLUSIVE: ICE NABS MULTIPLE CONVICTED KILLERS IN SINGLE DAY AMID NATIONWIDE IMMIGRATION SWEEP

DHS supplied Fox News Digital with five examples of people it identified as illegal immigrants arrested by ICE in California:

DHS UNLOADS ON TEACHERS UNION BOSS OVER 'DANGEROUS RHETORIC' AND ANTI-ICE ACTIVISM

These protests come as LAUSD continues to face widespread academic shortfalls, with most students tested falling below state standards in math and English. The district's 2026 assessment results showed roughly seven in ten 11th graders did not meet math standards, including nearly half who scored in the lowest achievement category.

The district reported a third consecutive year of improvement, with the share meeting or exceeding standards rising 1.88 percentage points in English and 2.98 points in math. Superintendent Andrés E. Chait emphasized the district’s responsibility to provide academic support when announcing the results.

"Our responsibility is to make sure every student has access to excellent teaching, meaningful academic support, and the opportunities they need to thrive," Chait said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, Los Angeles Mayor-elect Nithya Raman and LAUSD for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: IIHF website taken offline after reported hacking after Canada banned Russia from World Juniors
item.description: The International Ice Hockey Federation site went offline after a reported hack, as Canada says Russian athletes are unwelcome for World Junior Championship.
item.content:encoded:
The International Ice Hockey Federation was offline Tuesday after a reported hacking incident after Russia was banned from entering Canada for the upcoming World Junior Championship.

According to TSN, a message supported Russia's involvement in international tournaments, including next month's tournament. Alongside it was a picture of Russian players.

The IIHF site was still offline as of noon ET, with a message saying that it's temporarily offline and that they are "currently performing maintenance. Please check back later."

RUSSIA'S INTERNATIONAL HOCKEY BAN LIFTED, PROMPTING BACKLASH FROM IIHF, OTHER COUNTRIES: 'INCOMPREHENSIBLE'

OutKick has reached out to the IIHF for comment but has yet to hear back.

This comes as tensions are rising between the IIHF and Russia ahead of the World Juniors.

Russia has been barred from IIHF competition since the invasion of Ukraine; however, a ruling from the Court of Arbitration for Sport this year called for the country to be reinstated.

HOCKEY GREAT WAYNE GRETZKY DEFENDS RELATIONSHIP WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP AND SPEAKS ON RUSSIAN HOCKEY BAN

However, Canada — which is hosting the World Juniors in Edmonton and Red Deer — has said that the Russian team is not welcome at the upcoming tournament.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal and unjustified horrific war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said. "So, if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there."

Sweden, Finland, the Czech Republic, Norway, Latvia, and Denmark have all put out statements about boycotting games against Russia. Additionally, one of the tournament's top sponsors, STRAUSS, threatened to pull out if the Russian team was part of the tournament.

Russia's last World Juniors appearance came at the 2021 tournament, which, coincidentally, was also held in Edmonton and Red Deer. That year, the team came in fourth place, losing to Finland in the bronze medal game.

item.title: Obama-appointed judge paves way to unseal Ilhan Omar search warrant in blow to Trump's DOJ
item.description: A federal judge in Washington, D.C., paved the way to unseal the criminal search warrant and related documents against Rep. Ilhan Omar.
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. who has often ruled against the Trump administration dealt a blow to the Justice Department Tuesday, paving the way to unseal the criminal search warrant and related documents against Rep. Ilhan Omar. 

Judge James Boasberg, who was appointed to the bench by former President Barack Obama in 2011, asked the DOJ's attorneys to submit proposed redactions to the documents to the court by Friday, and said he plans to unseal some materials Monday. Any parts of the warrant or related materials that are not submitted with redactions on Friday will be released, he said. 

While criminal warrants aren't typically unsealed until after charges are filed, 15 media organizations and watchdog group Judicial Watch sued to obtain the warrant. They have argued that releasing the contents of the warrant is in the public interest.

'RADICAL LEFT LUNATIC' JUDGE TRUMP WANTED IMPEACHED TAKES UP ILHAN OMAR WARRANT FIGHT

The plaintiffs argued specifically that it should be made public which statutes federal investigators think Omar may have broken. 

Boasberg signaled that he would not release the warrant application, which is a sworn statement submitted to a judge explaining facts and evidence that establish probable cause for issuing a warrant.

The DOJ did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. 

Omar is facing a probe related to whether she or her father fraudulently filled out immigration paperwork in order for her to obtain citizenship. The Somali-born congresswoman said last week that she wasn't privy to what exactly the DOJ is investigating.

During the raid, which was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations (HIS), Omar's personal cellphone, computer and passport were seized. Her DNA has also been obtained, and her sister, Sahra Noor, was questioned by investigators the week of the raid.

FEDERAL AGENTS SEIZE PHONE OF REP ILHAN OMAR IN RAID TIED TO IMMIGRATION FRAUD PROBE

In a motion seeking to prevent the federal search warrant for the congresswoman’s home from being unsealed, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia referred to Omar as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar…" and sources later told Fox News Digital that Ilhan Omar is not the congresswoman's "real name."

That news caused speculation that Omar married her brother, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, to resurface. The pair married in 2009, and officially divorced in 2017.

ILHAN OMAR APPEARS CLUELESS ON BASIS FOR FEDERAL PROBES: ‘YOU PROBABLY HAVE MORE DETAILS ON THAT’

Omar has not been charged with a crime and has repeatedly and categorically denied any wrongdoing. She has characterized the investigation as politically motivated, saying President Donald Trump is targeting her.

But the DOJ under former President Barack Obama opened an investigation into Omar's marriage with Nur Said Elmi in 2016 — suggesting the nonpartisan nature of some of the inquiries into the Minnesota lawmaker.

OBAMA BACKS ILHAN OMAR AMID PROBE, ACCUSES TRUMP ADMIN OF 'APPALLING' TARGETING IN LENGTHY STATEMENT

The New York Times first reported that Obama's FBI and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) began the probe in the summer of 2016, and that officials "found some evidence that [the marriage] was fraudulent." The Times reported that the investigation concluded when officials decided the potential felony crime was past the statute of limitations.

That probe, an official told Fox News Digital, remained open until 2021, when it was closed under the Biden administration.

item.title: Dan Dakich goes to bat for Indiana's Curt Cignetti after coach rips CFP selection committee
item.description: Indiana Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti says the College Football Playoff committee's lack of respect "feeds into" IU's motivation ahead of selection.
item.content:encoded:
Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti sure knows how to work a microphone.

The 2025 national championship winning coach has always been somewhat of a lightning rod, even during his first press conference in Bloomington when he told reporters to "Google him" for his winning ways.

He can be quite the polarizing figure, prompting many to bristle at his candor and gruff nature while others appreciate the authenticity.

His latest comments have gotten plenty of people to react accordingly as well, with the Hoosiers head man taking the College Football Playoff selection committee to task for their perceived slights towards IU.

Cignetti told reporters at his Monday press conference that the lack of respect "feeds into (Indiana's) motivation," and that if anyone has a problem with him, he doesn't care.

HERE'S HOW BAD THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF'S SELECTION COMMITTEE RANKINGS ACTUALLY ARE | IAN MILLER

"I'm 65 years old," Cignetti responded dryly. "I don't give a s—."

One man who is absolutely loving what Cig is offering up to the press is OutKick's Dan Dakich.

DAN DAKICH REACTS TO MS NOW HOST JOE SCARBOROUGH'S PAT MCAFEE TAKE: 'THEY LOOK LIKE IDIOTS'

Dakich reacted to the quotes on the latest episode of "Don't @ Me," and couldn't have been more thrilled with how coach Cignetti is handling things at his alma mater.

"That is my mantra," Dakich said with a grin.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Although Cignetti's comments caused many on social media to clutch their pearls, Dakich doubled down and called out the reporters who had a problem with them.

"We want coaches to say things, but when they say things we cry like p—-es," Dakich retorted.

"Cignetti spoke for an entire generation when he said (that)."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Dakich also points out that Cignetti obviously cares what people think - otherwise he wouldn't have addressed it - but that this felt like a boiling point for the Indiana head coach.

"You see all these narratives out there attacking you," Dakich admits. "And what do you do? You attack back."

One thing is for sure, Cignetti is a competitive person, but as long as he keeps winning, he can say whatever he wants.

I'm sure Hoosiers fans don't mind one bit, and the results speak for themselves.

item.title: Veteran pilot: Congress must act to update 'archaic' FAA tech that is 'putting Americans in danger'
item.description: Retired Air Force pilot Buzz Patterson warns the FAA ground stop will happen again, blaming "tribal" politics for delaying a $50 billion modernization.
item.content:encoded:
Friday's historic FAA ground stop will not be the last, a retired Air Force veteran and commercial pilot warns, unless Congress takes action and provides funds for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to update what he calls a "broken" and "archaic" system that is "putting Americans in danger."

"It's time for both parties to step up and say our AT system is degraded, it's old," retired Lt. Col. Buzz Patterson, who carried the nuclear football for former President Bill Clinton and is a retired 16-year Delta Air Lines pilot, told Fox News Digital in an interview this week.

"We're putting Americans in danger when they get into an airplane, and we're putting the air crews in danger when they get into an airplane, if we continue to fly under archaic system, and that's what we're doing right now, it's archaic."

FORMER TOP FAA OFFICIAL WARNS OF 48-HOUR RECOVERY AFTER AGING TECH 'OVERWHELMED' AHEAD OF GROUND STOP

Too many administrations from both parties have "kicked the can" down the road on the complex and pricy overhaul, according to Patterson.

"We've dug a big hole here, and we're trying to dig out of it," he said. "It's not going to take place overnight. It's going to be a long, grinding, devoted effort, and I think it's time for our politicians to get on board and fix it."

TRUMP'S $50B AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL OVERHAUL FACES GOP PUSHBACK AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

Patterson, who just moved to Nevada and bought a new home he is renovating, said the $50 billion cost now laid bare by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy this weekend is akin to buying a home and immediately renovating it: Double down for the long-term benefits, if not savings.

"Our technology, I mean, we're still using floppy disks, for God's sakes, in some of our facilities," Patterson lamented. "Last time I was in a tower, they were still using paper scripts to show what airplanes were supposed to taxi next. This should all be automated ... I mean, this should be easy-peasy, and we've made it so difficult."

"We have way, way too much traffic to have an antiquated 1970s technology trying to drive our airplanes around the skies," he added, noting he "can't tell you the number of traffic avoidance calls I've gotten from ATC over the years that if I had not heard them, I probably would have hit somebody, or they would have hit me: so, it's essential."

Patterson, who now flies frequently as a commercial passenger himself, stressed that aviation safety transcends party lines and urged Washington to abandon what he called "tribal" politics to pass comprehensive modernization funding.

"It should be bipartisan, because I think if only one party pushes it, tries to push it through, it's not going to have success," he said. "I don't care what your political affiliation is: If you want to fly safely in our country, regardless of where you're going, or who you are, then you should be able to. And right now I think it's become tribal, where Democrats don't want to do anything that supports Trump or the FAA, and Trump's trying to get some stuff done."

BUTTIGIEG TAKES SWIPE AT TRUMP ADMINISTRATION AMID FAA FLIGHT CHAOS

Even President Donald Trump is "late" to conduct the overdue modernization, but he is also facing congressional gridlock, too, Patterson lamented.

"He's late, granted, he's late, but every other president's been late too – and so Duffy asking for $50 billion, I understand that is probably too little, too late, but it's a start."

While praising the dedication of current air traffic controllers and flight crews, Patterson warned that human skill can only compensate for technological limitations for so long. He noted that pilots still rely heavily on traditional voice radio relays rather than seamless, automated cockpit-to-ground data and weather integration, recalling numerous midair traffic avoidance calls from controllers over his career that prevented potential collisions.

BUTTIGIEG TRASHES DUFFY’S GROUND STOP RESPONSE, BUT HIS DOT FAILURES DOOM HIS 2028 BID

Patterson said weather radar, FAA and ATC can all be upgraded to improve airline safety, noting the recent Learjet 60 crash in Florida.

"You don't fly through that stuff, you just don't," Patterson said of the Learjet 60 crash that featured pilots seeking a direct route through a thunderstorm. "If you do, you're going realize why you don't, because it's going to bang the crap out of you if you get through it. And in this, in this case, they didn't get through it."

FLORIDA PLANE CRASH INVESTIGATORS SAY WEATHER CONDITIONS A 'MAJOR FOCUS,' PLANE MAY HAVE STARTED TO BREAK UP

Communications, weather radar, routers and copper to fiber optic wiring upgrades all go hand-in-hand for safety, according to Patterson.

"There is an interconnectivity between the National Weather Service and the FAA," he said. "There's an interconnectivity there that could be had if we upgrade our ATC capabilities, and we can somehow connect.

"And it shouldn't be too hard to connect the National Weather Service directly to the cockpit, and I think that's where we're going to have to go, and I think that's necessary. And it's also not ironic that the same day ATC went down, the National Weather Service went down. I'm not saying it was a coordinated activity. I'm just saying that is the basis of our aviation system.

"And if we don't have the most advanced air traffic control technology and the most advanced weather technology, then we, as the world's superpower, we have failed dramatically, and I think that's where we are."

DUFFY: INVESTIGATORS EXAMINING 2 ROUTERS AFTER NATIONWIDE FAA GROUND STOP, NO SIGNS OF FOREIGN CYBERATTACK

With peak holiday travel approaching, Patterson warned that systemic meltdowns will continue to disrupt the flying public until Washington commits to a sustained, multiyear overhaul.

"I'm going to say this won't be the last one; it's going happen again," Patterson said of the nationwide ground stop. "It's probably going happen on Thanksgiving Eve or Christmas Eve, and people are going to wonder why it's happening, and I'm going tell you why it's happening: It's because our infrastructure is broken, and our ATC needs help, and the FAA needs help."

"I think Sean Duffy is doing a phenomenal job," he concluded. "He's done more as a DOT guy than anybody that I can possibly remember since I started flying, and I think that what we're seeing right now is decades of neglect on the part of both parties. I mean, I'm not going to absolve Republicans either, because I'm looking at this as a pilot and as an American with a family, and I want to be able to fly my family safely around the country, and I don't feel safe putting my family on an airplane right now until we figure this out."

item.title: Ex-hostage recounts captivity in Iran-backed militia stronghold now targeted by Iraqi prime minister
item.description: Israeli-Russian researcher Elizabeth Tsurkov describes where Iran-backed Iraqi terrorists held her captive for months as Iraq's Trump-backed prime minister orders a crackdown on the militia.
item.content:encoded:
An Israeli-Russian researcher held hostage for 903 days by an Iran-backed Iraqi terrorist group revealed to Fox News Digital that she spent the first four and a half months of her captivity inside the very militia stronghold Iraq's Trump-backed prime minister has now ordered the army to reclaim.

Elizabeth Tsurkov, a senior nonresident fellow at the New Lines Institute for Strategy and Policy, said Kata’ib Hezbollah turned a private family's home in Jurf al-Sakhr, south of Baghdad, into a prison where she was held captive.

"This is where I was held for 4.5 months," Tsurkov told Fox News Digital in an interview, referring to the early months of her captivity, which began with her abduction in Baghdad in March 2023. "I was held in a private home of a family that was taken over by Kata’ib Hezbollah and turned into a prison," she said.

TRUMP ADMIN WARNS IRAQ OVER IRAN TERROR PROXIES AS US REPORTEDLY BLOCKS CASH PAYMENTS

Tsurkov, who was freed in September 2025 following negotiations and sustained pressure from the Trump administration to secure her release, said that any effort to reclaim the territory must go far beyond dismantling alleged oil-smuggling operations.

She called for Iraqi authorities to search the sprawling area, including surrounding towns and villages, for "secret prisons," "mass burial sites" and "storage facilities for weapons," and to return confiscated homes to their rightful owners.

The revelations come as Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who has received strong public backing from President Donald Trump, ordered Iraqi armed forces into Jurf al-Sakhr, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, a stronghold of the U.S.-designated terrorist organization Kata’ib Hezbollah since 2014.

According to AFP on November 16, Baghdad has given the militia a deadline to withdraw, with a security source identifying Friday.

The order follows a Reuters investigation published Monday, citing Iraqi officials who accused Kata’ib Hezbollah of stealing hundreds of millions of dollars in state-owned oil since 2021. The government has dismissed nine security and administrative officials and referred suspects to the judiciary. The militia denies wrongdoing.

IRAN’S PROXY WAR HAS CROSSED OCEANS AND IS NOW KNOCKING ON AMERICA’S DOOR

For Tsurkov, the stakes go far beyond oil revenues.

She described Jurf al-Sakhr as a territory effectively closed to the Iraqi government since 2014, when Iran-backed militias helped drive ISIS from the area but prevented its predominantly Sunni population from returning.

Tsurkov estimated that between 120,000 and 180,000 people were displaced from the district and surrounding communities. "If Iraqis are allowed to return to their homes, this would signal ... restitution of state sovereignty," she said.

She explained that the current operation is being presented as an anti-corruption campaign rather than an attempt to dismantle Kata’ib Hezbollah's military infrastructure.

The organization retains bases elsewhere in Iraq and access to border crossings with Iran, she said, giving it opportunities to replenish its weapons even if it loses control of Jurf al-Sakhr.

IRAN-BACKED TERROR SUSPECTS PLOTTED ATTACK ON US TROOPS USING VANS PACKED WITH FUEL, DOJ SAYS

Michael Knights, head of research at Horizon Engage, a New York-based strategic consultancy, and an adjunct fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, expressed skepticism that Baghdad would fundamentally challenge the militias.

"It's going to be very difficult to tell the difference between a real crackdown on Iran-backed militias and a fake one," Knights told Fox News Digital.

Previous Iraqi governments have announced crackdowns on militias, only for detainees to be released or armed groups to retain control through rebranded security arrangements.

In June 2020, when then-Prime Minister Mustafa al-Kadhimi ordered the arrest of 14 Kata’ib Hezbollah members. Armed militia supporters subsequently descended on Baghdad's fortified International Zone demanding their release. Most were later released, according to a U.S. government inspector general report.

In Nov. 2021, Kadhimi survived an explosive-drone attack targeting his residence. Reuters reported that security officials implicated Iran-backed militias, although no organization claimed responsibility.

Knights said that the Iraqi counterterrorism forces are better trained and equipped than Kata’ib Hezbollah, but the greatest danger lies in the militias' ability to threaten officials and their families.

"It's not about equipment or even training," he said, describing the danger of retaliation against commanders and their families who challenge the armed groups.

In a Nov. 16 Middle East Forum analysis, researcher Ali Mahmoud detailed competing allegations of corruption between Kata’ib Hezbollah and Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq, including claims involving companies connected to militia leaders' families.

Mahmoud reported that even the government's initial inspection of Jurf al-Sakhr required negotiations with senior militia commanders, illustrating the limits of Baghdad's authority.

IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS

Tsurkov, who has researched Iraqi armed groups for years, said her captivity gave her unusual insight into the organization's internal culture.

"I interacted with about 45 different individuals across basically three different prisons," she said, explaining that she later supplemented those observations with interviews involving former militia members and people familiar with their communities.

Her conclusion was that the organization consists of both deeply committed Iranian loyalists and a much larger group of recruits primarily motivated by salaries, status and the ability to exercise power. "They enjoy having power over others," she said, describing what she observed among her captors.

While some members embrace Iran's revolutionary ideology, Tsurkov said many joined after the major fighting against ISIS ended, attracted by government-funded salaries and relatively secure employment. "They're not interested in dying in the service of the Iranian regime," she said of many rank-and-file fighters.

She distinguished those recruits from a smaller core of ideologically committed and better-trained operatives that Iran can mobilize for sophisticated military attacks.

That distinction, she said, could offer Baghdad a path toward reducing militia power without a full-scale confrontation. She proposed allowing some fighters to join the regular Iraqi army under independent military commanders, providing alternative employment while dismantling their existing command structures.

US FACES ANOTHER MAJOR MIDDLE EAST TROOP WITHDRAWAL, BUT THREAT REMAINS

According to Knights, the current crackdown primarily affects the more confrontational Abu Hussein wing of Kata’ib Hezbollah, while another faction associated with senior militia commander Abu Fadak remains largely untouched. He argued that both ultimately remain responsive to Tehran.

Knights also questioned whether disrupting one oil-smuggling operation would substantially weaken the group's finances, citing its extensive investments in hotels, property and other commercial ventures.

But perhaps the clearest illustration of the contradictions facing Iraq's government, Knights said, lies in recent senior political appointments and Iran's choice of its next diplomatic representative in Baghdad.

On Oct. 15, Iraq's parliament approved Laith al-Khazali, a senior figure in the Iran-backed Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq militia, as one of three deputy prime ministers. The United States designated him and his brother Qais al-Khazali, the militia's leader, as specially designated global terrorists in 2020. Washington has accused the organization of carrying out attacks against American and coalition forces, according to al-Monitor.

IRAN'S SHADOW OPERATIONS STRETCH ACROSS EUROPE AS CHILLING SPY CONVICTIONS EXPOSE TEHRAN'S REACH

Another newly appointed deputy prime minister, Muhsin al-Mandalawi, is the brother of two Iraqi businessmen sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury Department on Sept. 10 for facilitating financial transactions benefiting Iran. Knights also pointed to Iran's reported selection of Abdolreza Meskarian, a senior commander in the Revolutionary Guards' Quds Force, as its next ambassador to Iraq.

Alhurra reported on Nov. 9, citing an Iraqi Foreign Ministry source, that Tehran nominated Meskarian, who heads the Quds Force's Ramadan Headquarters, a unit involved in coordinating with Iran-backed armed groups in Iraq. Neither government had formally confirmed the nomination.

For Knights, these developments raise fundamental questions about how far Baghdad is prepared to go in challenging Tehran's influence. "I think on balance, we're still in a pretty bad place in Iraq when it comes to militias," he said.

IRAN’S PROXY MONEY MACHINE: HOW THE HOUTHIS BUILT A MULTIBILLION-DOLLAR NETWORK DESPITE US SANCTIONS

Tsurkov agreed that an operation intended merely to satisfy Washington could be exposed if displaced families remained unable to return.

The broader disarmament deadline, already extended until June 2027, was "utterly unrealistic," she said, arguing that Iraqi security institutions would require years of reform before they could reliably confront the militias.

"I tend to think it will not be real," she said of the current operation, while acknowledging that successful government control could represent a meaningful breakthrough.

For the former hostage, the ultimate measure of success is straightforward: whether Iraq's military merely enters the area, or whether the territory truly returns to civilian control.

"It's either the state is there, and people can return or not," she said.

Knights also remains skeptical that the current operation will deliver lasting results, suggesting Baghdad may reach a deal that allows the government to claim victory without substantially weakening Kata’ib Hezbollah. Still, he acknowledged the possibility that the confrontation could mark the beginning of a broader effort, even if he doubts this particular operation will prove decisive. "Every great journey starts with the first step," he said.

item.title: Adam Copeland reportedly fought off a bear while walking his dogs before AEW Full Gear
item.description: Adam Copeland says he kicked a mother bear under the jaw while walking his dogs, then told people his shin was hurt before facing Kazuchika Okada.
item.content:encoded:
AEW star Adam Copeland's toughest battle recently didn’t take place inside a wrestling ring. It took place in a residential neighborhood while he was minding his own business and walking his dogs.

He was reportedly approached by a mother bear and her cubs last week prior to AEW Full Gear, which took place on Saturday, Nov. 14, in Phoenix, Arizona. According to Bryan Alvarez of F4WOnline, he won the fight with the bear.

Copeland, unable to make himself as big as possible in an attempt to scare the bear off due to holding onto his dogs' leashes, didn’t have many options but to defend himself with his legs. And that's exactly what he did, Alvarez says.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

As the bear continued to approach him, Alvarez says Copeland kicked it with his shin under the bear's jaw. That ended what could have been a much nastier fight.

The bear backed off and the wrestler and his dogs weren't harmed. Well, they weren't harmed any worse than the damage done to a shin from kicking a bear under its jaw.

Copeland was said to have been telling people before he stepped into the ring with Kazuchika Okada that his shin was hurt due to kicking the bear. He did end up losing the match to Okada.

If you have to pick one of these fights to lose, it's obviously the one inside a wrestling ring, even with the International Championship on the line.

Don't get me wrong, an International Championship would have been nice.

But losing to a bear can ruin much more than a weekend in November and you don't need a story about a pro wrestler winning his fight with a bear to know that.

item.title: Sen Rand Paul and Sen-elect Andy Barr back Rep James Comer for Kentucky governor
item.description: Sen. Rand Paul and Rep. Andy Barr both backed Rep. James Comer for Kentucky governor after the congressman announced a gubernatorial bid.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., and Sen.-elect Andy Barr, R-Ky., are both backing Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., for Kentucky governor.

"I’m proud to endorse my friend @JamesComer to be Kentucky’s next Governor! Please help him to get there!" Paul declared in a Monday night post on X.

Barr, a House Republican who just won a U.S. Senate contest during the midterms, also threw his support behind Comer's candidacy.

JAMES COMER LAUNCHES BID FOR KENTUCKY GOVERNOR

"No one will fight harder for Kentucky families, Kentucky farmers, and Kentucky's future than my friend James Comer. Kentucky conservatives have built a strong legislature, and now we need a Governor who will work with them, not against them," Barr said in a Tuesday statement.

"With James Comer in the Governor's mansion, we'll finish the job on eliminating the state income tax and unleash Kentucky energy producers to lower costs and create jobs. I'm proud to stand with James Comer for Governor," he added.

MASSIE'S PUSH TO IMPEACH HEGSETH SPLITS CONSTITUENTS IN HIS OWN BACKYARD: 'PURE SPITE'

Comer, who has served in the House of Representatives for a decade, just won re-election during the midterms. The lawmaker, who chairs the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, announced a Bluegrass State gubernatorial bid on Monday.

He previously ran for Kentucky governor in 2015, but lost the GOP gubernatorial primary by only 83 votes.

The state's 2027 race for governor will take place in slightly less than a year, and the primary is set for May 18.

GOP FISCAL HAWK SOUNDS ALARM ON 'OUT OF CONTROL' FEDERAL SPENDING, SAYING 'BOTH PARTIES HAVE FAILED US'

Current Gov. Andy Beshear, a Democrat who is currently serving his second term, is ineligible to serve a third-consecutive term. Kentucky's state constitution stipulates, "The Governor shall be ineligible for the succeeding four years after the expiration of any second consecutive term for which he shall have been elected."

item.title: Sherrill commits $20.2M to deportation defense while condemning Rutgers over Border Patrol speaker
item.description: Mikie Sherrill condemned Rutgers College Republicans over a Gregory Bovino event while pouring $20.2 million into New Jersey's deportation defense program.
item.content:encoded:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill put her money where her mouth was this week as the Democrat criticized Rutgers University’s College Republican chapter for hosting a top former Border Patrol leader around the same time her administration allocated millions to a program meant to help illegal immigrants and others in the state fight deportation.

Sherrill’s condemnation of the Rutgers students’ event drew criticism on X from observers who said it fueled protests outside the New Brunswick building where retired Border Patrol Cmdr. Gregory Bovino spoke. Protests erupted inside the room as well, with video from inside showing Bovino responding to shouting protesters before he was briefly led out of the forum.

"Everyone in this country is entitled to due process and a fair hearing under the law — regardless of where they were born," Sherrill said Friday in announcing a total of $20.2 million to fund the Detention Deportation Defense Initiative within Trenton’s Office of New Americans.

NJ TAXPAYERS ON THE HOOK FOR $12M MORE AS DEM GOVERNOR PROTECTS ILLEGAL ALIENS BATTLING DEPORTATION

Some of the funds will help migrants held at Delaney Hall in Essex County, where nightly protests have erupted since May. The governor previously visited the facility in solidarity with the detainees inside, while Sherrill ally Sen. Andy Kim, D-N. J., drew widespread attention online after being caught in a cloud of pepper spray dispersed by ICE toward surrounding protesters.

"With the Trump Administration ramping up ICE activity and creating impossible obstacles for people facing detention and deportation to navigate alone, New Jersey is stepping up to connect residents with qualified legal counsel and equip more attorneys to take on this vital work," Sherrill said Friday, adding that the state’s immigrant community should not have to face a "complex" legal system alone.

Commissioner Stephen Cha, head of Sherrill’s Department of Human Services, where the Office of New Americans sits, added in a statement that access to legal representation upholds due process and promotes a more "efficient" immigration system.

The $20.2 million will be spread among 10 service providers and continue the Murphy-era initiative’s mission to offer legal expertise and representation for "low-income residents facing detention and deportation."

EXCLUSIVE VIDEO: DEMS SLAMMED FOR DEMANDING ‘FIVE-STAR ACCOMMODATIONS’ FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS AT ICE FACILITY

Sherrill’s new cash infusion tripled the initiative’s most recent budget allocation.

After Sherrill announced plans in June to increase the deportation defense initiative’s funding, Republicans in the state warned that the money could be better spent elsewhere, including on New Jersey residents.

"New Jersey families are being crushed by some of the highest electric bills, property taxes, and costs of living in the entire country, and Governor Sherrill's answer is to spend more than $20 million defending illegal immigrants," said outgoing Rep. Jeff Van Drew, R-N.J., who was unseated by Cape May Mayor Zachary Mullock in this month’s blue wave.

"It is a complete insult to every hardworking taxpayer in this state. New Jersey citizens should come first. If they can find $20 million for immigration lawyers, they can find money to lower utility delivery charges or provide relief to the people who actually live, work and pay taxes here."

Van Drew said in June that every dollar Trenton spends on an illegal immigrant is a dollar that could have helped keep a New Jersey family from leaving the state.

A DHS spokesperson said Sherrill has "consistently shown more concern for criminal illegal aliens who've broken our laws and destroyed any possibility of ever remaining in our country than she ever has for Rachel Morin, Laken Riley, Jocelyn Nungaray and the true victims of illegal alien crimes in America," while adding it does not comment specifically on matters involving former personnel like Bovino.

Fox News Digital reached out to Sherrill for comment.

Sherrill had publicly condemned Bovino and Rutgers’ College Republicans for holding the event.

Rutgers is New Jersey’s state university, and the governor appoints some of its board members. Delaware Valley radio host Rich Zeoli said the state gives the New Brunswick school about $1.4 billion annually, adding the argument can be made she is "using a classic intimidation tactic to silence speech she doesn't like."

MARKWAYNE MULLIN GOES OFF ON DEMS’ 'GARBAGE' MEMORIAL DAY ‘POLITICAL STUNT’ AT ICE FACILITY

Sherrill urged attendees to press Bovino on why he chooses "cruelty over humanity" and what he thinks of the November election results and the argument that they represent a collective rebuke of his enforcement approach.

The North Carolina native shot back at Sherrill, saying her statement was "spoken like a true lib who puts illegal aliens before her own citizens."

"Gubner, I am deeply disappointed in your penchant for using the Governor’s Office to limit Constitutional rights of Americans," Bovino said in a statement.

"This coming from someone who cheated at the Naval Academy (you weren’t allowed to walk), and enriched yourself via insider trading in defense stocks as a Congressgirl — priceless." Sherrill has said she was barred from walking at the graduation not because she was involved in cheating but because she declined to identify classmates involved.

New Jersey State Assemblyman Paul Kanitra, R-Point Pleasant Beach, said Sherrill’s criticism of Bovino contrasts with her silence over Democrats electing a candidate in the state who was once acquaintances with the mastermind behind the 1993 World Trade Center bombing.

"The thought-police strike again," Kanitra said.

"I didn’t see you weighing in when any Adam Hamawy said some pretty heinous things recently? That didn’t seem to warrant a tweet," he said, referring to the Mercer County doctor and former defense trial witness for the Blind Sheikh who won the race to succeed retiring Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman, D-N.J.

Hamawy was never charged with any wrongdoing in connection with Abdel-Rahman, and his campaign previously told Fox News Digital related criticisms amount to "guilt-by-association" shaming and that Republicans and right-wing press are simply concerned that Hamawy will be "Donald Trump's worst nightmare."

Bovino later challenged Sherrill to attend his event, which the governor did not attend.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Tell you what, come on down to Rutgers and put your insider-trading money where your mouth is. You won’t be able to cheat your way through this one."

Sherrill’s 2025 gubernatorial campaign previously denied the stock-trading allegation raised by Bovino, which stemmed from Republican challenger Jack Ciattarelli’s claim that she "cash[ed] in to the tune of $7 million" by "flipping stocks" while in Congress.

item.title: Mamdani takes swipe at Trump administration's response to tech outages: 'Far from what many wanted to hear'
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Tuesday blasted the federal government's response to multiple technical outages that impacted Americans.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani took a swipe at the Trump administration Tuesday following days of tech outages sweeping the nation, saying that "the response that we heard from federal officials was far from what many wanted to hear."

Mamdani spoke after the U.S. experienced a slew of technology disruptions that halted flights, email services and online banking platforms across the country.

"What I will say to New Yorkers is both an understanding of their frustration, we are speaking about New Yorkers who had made plans for months, some of them years, about going on a trip with their family or coming home from a trip with their family. And frankly, the response that we heard from federal officials was far from what many wanted to hear," Mamdani said.

"And it did not leave many New Yorkers with any greater sense of confidence about our national capabilities in case of this occurring again," he continued. "And I'm looking forward to seeing Democratic majorities in the House and the Senate utilize that power to also ensure that we're delivering more answers at a national level, because what we were hearing from some of the secretaries that day was in no way confidence building."

DUFFY VOWS TO MODERNIZE AGING AIR TRAFFIC SYSTEM AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

Fox News Digital has reached out to the White House for comment.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said two routers from Federal Aviation Administration facilities in Texas and Arkansas are undergoing extensive testing as investigators examine whether faulty equipment or an installation problem triggered the nation's longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years this past Friday.

The shutdown occurred as contractor L3Harris was replacing aging copper wiring with fiber-optic technology in the FAA's communications system.

Duffy then said during an appearance on Fox News' "Hannity" Monday that he plans to modernize America’s aging air traffic control system and build new architecture that is "worthy of America." The secretary also said intelligence agencies found no evidence of a cyberattack.

DHS CHIEF TELLS AMERICANS TO 'BREATHE' AMID TECH OUTAGES, INSISTS HOMELAND IS 'SECURE'

The roughly five-hour ground stop affected more than 1.5 million passengers whose flights were scheduled to depart on Friday afternoon and evening. More than 12,000 flights were canceled that day, according to the FAA, while delays and cancellations continued through the weekend.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said Monday on "Hannity" that "the homeland is secure.

"Our banking system is secure and when something like this happens, we’re able to react and react fast," Mullin continued.

Mullin’s remarks came as customers Monday reported trouble accessing online services of major U.S. banking platforms, including Wells Fargo, Chase, U.S. Bank and Bank of America. United Airlines also faced a widespread system outage on Monday that briefly affected departing flights.

Mullin maintained that the incidents were not a result of cyberattacks and described the disruptions as "individually unrelated."

Fox News Digital's Nora Moriarty, Stephen Sorace and Landon Mion contributed to this report.

item.title: Spartans look to exploit Tennessee's thin frontcourt in a road college basketball battle
item.description: Michigan State basketball enters its clash with Tennessee at 4-0 after beating Duke, while the Volunteers are 3-0 and face their first real test.
item.content:encoded:
In any sport, the end goal is to win the championship. Every year we evaluate teams and make a list of how many could win the whole thing, and a few that might have a shot if everything goes right for them. With College Basketball, we’ve seen certain teams like Duke, UConn, and some others become part of the conversation annually. Then there are some random teams that are good, but might not be true contenders. It is too early, but I feel like both Michigan State and Tennessee fall into the good, but not contender category, and they square off today.

Michigan State is certainly one of the best teams in the country, and the Spartans come into the game with a 4-0 record, having won their first major test of the season. They’ve faced Quinnipiac, Toledo, Duke, and the University of Northern Iowa. As you would probably expect, the game against the Blue Devils was the only truly tough game of the season. They won their first two games by 30 or more points. Then they beat Duke by six at the United Center in Chicago. Against Northern Iowa, they won by 34.

Beating Duke is a big deal, and although it was a neutral court, the team did seem to have an advantage with the game being in Chicago – at least closer to its campus than to Duke’s. Michigan State is led by Jeremey Fears Jr., who is averaging 16.8 points per game, and he is averaging 10 assists as well. He is one of the better players in the nation, but he might fall into the "good in college, but not as good in the pros" category. We know the team will be well coached, and they have Fears, but my concern is that the team may not be deep enough against the better teams as the season goes on.

The Tennessee Volunteers are 3-0 for the season, and one of the top-ranked teams in the nation as well. This is certainly the first real test of their young season. They started the year against Wofford, winning by 31 points. Then they played Radford and won by 23. Tennessee may have been looking ahead a bit when facing Tennessee State in the last game because the Volunteers won by just five points against a truly inferior opponent. These things can happen when teams have a bigger game upcoming, but the Volunteers pulled it out either way, so it shouldn’t be held against them.

If the Volunteers can be exploited at any position, it is their front court. Although it is only three games, they have only one forward and one center in their top seven scorers. The two have combined to average 14 points per game for the Volunteers. Their five guards are averaging seven or more points, led by Terrence Hill Jr., who has 18 points per game. There isn’t much height on the team, so they have an issue there.

Tennessee would benefit from this being a faster-paced game. Michigan State will likely want to slow it down and take advantage of the team in the post. I’m curious to see how Tennessee battles on the boards in this game and in others. Being at home will give the Volunteers an edge in the game, but I think Michigan State is superior in the front court and its guards are good enough. Couple that with being tested already, and I’ll take the Spartans to cover the -2.5.

item.title: NASA investigates mysterious 'potato chip' shapes on Mars as scientists hunt for answers
item.description: NASA says its Curiosity rover is probing chip-shaped crystal formations in Martian bedrock at the Nazca site, using SAM and ChemCam to analyze their makeup.
item.content:encoded:
NASA scientists are investigating unusual "potato chip-shaped" formations on Mars as they seek to determine how these shapes formed — and just what they're made of, exactly.

The news was announced in NASA's "Curiosity" blog on Nov. 11.

Curiosity is a NASA rover that has been exploring Mars since 2012. It examined the unusual formations during a drilling campaign at a site nicknamed "Nazca" last week.

TREASURE HUNTER STRIKES GOLD WITH 1,000-YEAR-OLD DISCOVERY LINKED TO 'HAND OF GOD'

The Nazca drill site is located in a Martian area where scientists have observed unusual disk-shaped features in the bedrock.

"This is an area characterized by bedrock containing disk-shaped (or, in a liberal interpretation, potato-chip shaped) crystal forms," the NASA blog said.

Images of the Martian bedrock show irregular, curled formations embedded in the rock, some with shapes resembling potato chips.

PUZZLING SOUND IN BACKYARD LEADS HOMEOWNER TO MASSIVE 1,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE

NASA said one of its key objectives is to "better characterize these chip-shaped features."

Samples collected from the Nazca drill hole were delivered to Curiosity's Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument, an onboard laboratory designed to analyze the chemical makeup of Martian samples.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Curiosity also planned to use its laser-equipped ChemCam instrument to examine a crystal-shaped formation nicknamed "Colca" to gather information about its chemical composition.

Scientists also planned to use the Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), a camera mounted on Curiosity's robotic arm, to photograph the crystal-shaped formations at night using white-light and ultraviolet LED lamps.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"ChemCam LIBS observations were planned for each sol including a cluster of crystal forms, a resistant layer in the side of the Nazca block and a dark float rock," NASA's blog stated.

The rover was then expected to leave the Nazca drill site and return to its southward route to continue exploring Mars as part of its Friday plan.

Fox News Digital reached out to NASA to ask more about the chip-shaped formations and whether they've been observed before.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The unusual formations are among the latest objects being studied as scientists continue to explore Mars and other parts of the solar system.

Last month, astronomers discovered a potential dwarf planet beyond Pluto using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile.

The object, named 2026 ED138, is estimated to measure between 370 and 930 miles across, potentially making it one of the largest dwarf planets ever discovered in the distant solar system.

item.title: Ukraine releases video showing damage to Putin's prized bridge following 'unprecedented operation' in Crimea
item.description: Videos released by Ukrainian authorities show part of a key bridge in Crimea missing after the Kremlin claimed a drone attack only caused minor damage.
item.content:encoded:
The Security Service of Ukraine released two videos Tuesday showing the aftermath of a devastating drone attack on Russian President Vladimir Putin's prized Crimea bridge.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday's attack on the Kerch Strait bridge was part of an "unprecedented operation in response to Russian strikes on our infrastructure."

"Today, everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing from Russian territory into our Ukrainian Crimea," Zelenskky wrote on X. "This is the result of the seventh stage of an operation carried out over several weeks ... Our warriors gradually destroyed air defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective.

"Today, at the key stage, the 'Palianytsia' drones performed exceptionally well, striking the road section of the bridge, while 'Neptune' missiles, 'Ruta' drones, and FP-5 drones struck the railway section. Using 'Flamingo,' our warriors carried out a precision-guided strike – and the communications uplink worked flawlessly until the very last seconds," Zelenskyy added.

UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY'

Artem Dekhtyarenko, a spokesperson for the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), said Monday's strikes destroyed one of the bridge's two steel arches and the road span that was underneath it.

Footage released by Ukrainian authorities showed half of the bridge missing.

Russian-installed Crimean Governor Sergei Aksyonov confirmed that the Kerch Strait bridge, linking occupied Crimea to mainland Russia, had been struck. However, the Kremlin claimed the damage as minor.

FRENCH TROOPS SECRETLY DEPLOYED INSIDE UKRAINE AS EX-NATO CHIEF PRAISES MACRON'S 'GUTS'

The bridge is both a strategically important supply route and a symbol of Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea.

"We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation – and every proposal has been met with loud rejection," Zelenskyy said Tuesday.

"Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region. We are restoring our infrastructure. But we are also reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began," he added. "Ukraine’s defensive capabilities are strong and will remain so, and we will never leave terror against our cities and people unanswered."

Fox News' Thomas Ferraro, Efrat Lachter and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Jerry Jones says discussions about replacing the Cowboys' embattled defensive coordinator are underway
item.description: Jerry Jones says the Cowboys are discussing changes to Chris Parker's defensive coordinator role after a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
Change could be coming to the Dallas Cowboys coaching staff this week as discussions about adjusting defensive coordinator Chris Parker's role are underway, according to team owner Jerry Jones.

"We're talking about that," said Jones on his weekly segment on 105.3 The Fan in the Metroplex area on Tuesday morning. "But I'm not going to talk about it here. But we are talking about those things."

Jones also didn't wish to discuss whether Parker's scheme is being adjusted, probably in a manner that is simpler.

JERRY JONES SAYS COWBOYS COACH WON'T BE FIRED AFTER LOSS BUT INDY'S SHANE STEICHEN HAS NO SUCH PLEDGE MONDAY

"Those things are being aired out," Jones said before again adding he wasn't discussing the details on the radio.

The conversation about replacing Parker has been going on for some weeks as the Cowboys have struggled on the defensive side of the ball. But the chorus has reached a crescendo following Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in which the Cowboys simply embarrassed themselves on defense.

And Parker's calls were, well, highly questionable.

If the Cowboys make a change ahead of Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans or at any time, the obvious replacement for Parker is Mike Pettine.

The Cowboys added Pettine as a senior defensive assistant a few weeks ago. Unlike Parker, who is 34 and had never been a defensive coordinator before this season, Pettine has previously been a defensive coordinator for the New York Jets, Buffalo Bills, and Chicago Bears.

So why this internal discussion about Parker now? Well, the problem is obvious.

Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns against the 49ers and the Cowboys lost. The Cowboys this season have lost games despite scoring 31, 30 and 40 points.

"Something's gotta change," Prescott said after the loss.

Bobby Belt, who covers the Cowboys for 105.3 The Fan, has shared an eyebrow-raising statistic about the Dallas defense:

Dallas has allowed five pass plays of 50 yards or more in the last three weeks. The NFC's other 15 teams have in that same span allowed two plays of 50 yards or more.

Rex Ryan, who once upon a time was a defensive coordinator for the Baltimore Ravens before becoming a head coach with the New York Jets and Buffalo Bills, has been especially hard on Parker's work for the Cowboys.

"He's got no feel," Ryan said on ESPN on Tuesday. "Number one, the guy has no feel for the game. He doesn't know when to call things, when not to call things."

item.title: 'West Wing' star declares America has 60,000 people in internment camps on 'The View'
item.description: Bradley Whitford claimed on ABC's "The View" that 60,000 people are held in "internment camps," referencing ICE detention under the Trump administration.
item.content:encoded:
"West Wing" actor Bradley Whitford claimed that there are 60,000 people currently locked in "internment camps" in the U.S. during a Monday appearance on ABC's "The View."

During his appearance on the panel, Whitford said he was relieved by the election results, which he described as relegating an "authoritarian, cruel impulse" to the "ash heap of history." However, he said he still had concerns.

"I was looking today that...we have internment camps," Whitford said. "There are 60,000 people in internment camps. This is unacceptable aside from all the disastrous economic decisions that have been made. Children, 6,000 children."

MADDOW FEARS TRUMP MIGRANT DETENTION CENTERS MAY BE USED TO IMPRISON ‘THE REST OF US’

"The View" co-host Sunny Hostin agreed with Whitford, saying, "Yeah, we do."

Whitford appeared to be referring to reports that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) was holding approximately 60,000 people in detention centers as part of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. 

"Comparing ICE detention centers to World War II internment camps is disgusting," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. 

"No lawbreakers in human history have been better treated than illegal aliens in the U.S. These types of smears by Hollywood elites and the media are leading to our ICE law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,600% increase in assaults against them as they put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, terrorists, and gang members," she added. 

In his comments on "The View," Whitford did not directly compare ICE detention centers to World War II internment camps. 

Several critics of President Donald Trump have similarly compared immigration detention to the U.S. government's incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II.

ROSIE O’DONNELL RANTS THAT TRUMP-ERA ICE FACILITIES ARE CONCENTRATION CAMPS WHERE INMATES ARE RAPED

Fox News Digital reached out to Whitford, ICE, ABC for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Whitford, who has frequently criticized Trump and the Republican Party, also emphasized the importance of preserving democracy following the midterm elections.

"I think the whole way that we've gone under this threat to our democracy is because we assumed it was inevitable. And democracy is not inevitable. You've got to make it every damned day. And we need to continue to do it. It's still a very scary time," Whitford said.

'THE HANDMAID'S TALE' STAR RAGES AGAINST OLD BOSS JEFF BEZOS, TELLS HIM TO 'F------ SPEAK UP' AGAINST TRUMP

Whitford made similar comments on "The View" last year, where he lamented how "people are jumping out of vans, and people going through a legal asylum process are being taken away without charges." At the time, he said that his father, who fought in World War II, was "Antifa" for fighting fascism.

item.title: UFC's Bruce Buffer fuels speculation about another Conor McGregor comeback: 'Fighter mentality'
item.description: Bruce Buffer says Conor McGregor's warrior spirit means there's a very good chance he returns to the Octagon after his torn ACL against Max Holloway.
item.content:encoded:
Conor McGregor's UFC comeback did not go as he had hoped.

After five years without a fight, McGregor opened his July 11 fight against Max Holloway aggressively, attempting a running kick before throwing a head kick moments later. However, he slipped both times because it was apparent he had suffered a knee injury.

He tried to power through it, but nearly two minutes into the fight, he grabbed at his right leg again, and referee Mike Beltran called the fight after just 69 seconds following what ultimately was a torn ACL.

One may argue that the UFC is already in its post-McGregor era, but the Irishman has vowed he'll be back, and longtime UFC in-ring announcer Bruce Buffer seems to believe that is the case.

"The thing about Conor is that he’s a huge draw. We know that. He has a fighter mentality. With all the riches he’s achieved and everything else, that fighter mentality will never leave him. His warrior spirit will always be there," Buffer told OutKick in a recent interview.

"When he looks at fights, whether it’s his bare-knuckle event or the UFC, he envisions himself being in there. He loves the UFC and the UFC crowd. I can say that he’s thinking every day, 'I want to be back in the Octagon.' There’s a very good chance that we may see Conor one more time.

UFC RING ANNOUNCER BRUCE BUFFER, 69, HAS NO PLANS OF RETIREMENT ANY TIME SOON; WANTS 'TO KEEP GOING'

"You have crowds all over the world where, let’s say, half the crowd wants to see him win and half the people want to see him lose. That means everybody’s going to watch. That’s why he’s such a huge draw."

Shortly after the injury, an emotional McGregor said his "head gasket is gone."

"Destroyed. I had no injury / injuries going into the fight. I was throwing kicks, planted and jumping, all throughout camp as well as backstage before the fight. This came out of nowhere. I am beyond dark here. I can only describe it as hell," he said on X.

McGregor was participating in his first bout since July 2021 when he lost to Dustin Poirier due to a separate devastating leg injury. He’s only won one fight since 2020 but does have one more fight remaining on his UFC contract.

item.title: NSA's highly classified communications network disrupted by widespread outage
item.description: The National Security Agency's classified NSA Net faces an intermittent outage, with staggered arrivals preventing tens of thousands of logins at once.
item.content:encoded:
The National Security Agency's internal classified communications network is experiencing an "intermittent outage," but critical communications remain intact, a person familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

The disruption affects a highly classified network known as NSA Net, which agency personnel use to communicate classified information internally.

The latest impact at one of the nation's most sensitive intelligence agencies also comes amid a string of technology outages affecting major U.S. institutions, from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to Microsoft and major banks, raising fresh concerns about the reliability of critical communications infrastructure.

DHS CHIEF TELLS AMERICANS TO 'BREATHE' AMID TECH OUTAGES, INSISTS HOMELAND IS 'SECURE'

CNN first reported the outage Tuesday, citing five people familiar with the matter.

The agency has implemented staggered arrival times for personnel at NSA to prevent tens of thousands of employees from attempting to log into their computers simultaneously as officials work to address the disruption, the person familiar with the matter said.

The issue appears to be technical in nature, according to the source, though the precise cause has not been established.

Despite the disruption, the agency has not lost critical communications capabilities and has numerous backup facilities available to maintain operations, the source said.

DUFFY: INVESTIGATORS EXAMINING 2 ROUTERS AFTER NATIONWIDE FAA GROUND STOP, NO SIGNS OF FOREIGN CYBERATTACK

The NSA, which is responsible for collecting and analyzing foreign signals intelligence, plays a central role in supporting U.S. intelligence and military operations.

It remains unclear when the outage began or how long it will take to fully restore the affected network.

Fox News Digital reached out to the NSA for comment. 

The disruption comes amid a string of high-profile technology outages over the last week affecting government systems and major businesses.

On Friday, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop after a telecommunications failure disrupted aircraft communications and radar feeds. The agency said instability spread to 17 of its 22 air route traffic control centers before flights resumed later that evening.

The disruption was attributed by the FAA to excessive data flooding its aging telecommunications network, potentially originating from two facilities in Texas and Arkansas. Officials said they had found no indication of a cyberattack.

Federal authorities are separately warning of increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. In a Nov. 13 advisory, the FBI warned that hackers are exploiting an artificial intelligence-powered penetration testing framework known as ARTEX to automate attacks against organizations worldwide.

The FBI said the technology has allowed some attackers to move from initial targeting to privileged access in less than three hours. Microsoft previously linked the framework to a China-aligned hacking group's exploitation of a ConnectWise supply-chain compromise, which involved attempts to access more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 customer environments.

There is no evidence linking the NSA disruption to the ARTEX activity or the other recent outages.

item.title: Russell Brand sparks prison investigation after wife reads defiant message following rape conviction

Russell Brand's recent message from behind prison bars is being "urgently investigated" by authorities as the "appalling" move proves to have "broken the rules."

On Sunday, Brand — who was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault — claimed he is "not guilty" in a message read by his wife, Laura Brand, during an episode of the couple's weekly Sunday Service YouTube vlog.

Shortly after the message was shared publicly, a spokesperson for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, said in a statement to Deadline: "This is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he’s found to have broken the rules."

RUSSELL BRAND POLICE INTERROGATION VIDEO EMERGES AS NEW RAPE INVESTIGATIONS LOOM AFTER CONVICTION

"Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances. Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."

In the message, Brand claimed his innocence while confirming he is currently being jailed at Littlehey Prison, a prison for individuals who have been convicted of sexual offenses.

"Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening," Laura read from a notebook.

KATY PERRY'S COMMENT THAT EX 'SHOULD BE IN JAIL' RESURFACES AFTER RUSSELL BRAND'S PRISON SENTENCING

Brand was sentenced on Nov. 9.

During sentencing, Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand had demonstrated a "casual and arrogant disregard" for women’s right to refuse his sexual advances.

"About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous," Bennathan said. "You were clever — and in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator."

The judge described one of Brand’s sexual assaults as "outrageous and possibly laddish, but also a criminal offense," adding that Brand’s behavior reflected his belief that "fame meant you could act how you liked, when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live."
