According to Sky News, as Brand was taken from the dock by three guards, he turned to his wife and nodded, saying, "We'll be OK."

Laura reportedly mouthed back, "I love you, I'll be OK."

Brand has denied the charges and was acquitted of two additional rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

He was immediately taken into custody following the verdict, according to the BBC.

Brand, 51, was accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009.

In a video posted to X last year, Brand thanked his fans for messages of support, then criticized the British government and legal system before addressing the charges directly.

He said that he "was a fool before I lived in the light of the Lord. I was a drug addict, a sex addict and an imbecile, but what I never was was a rapist. I've never engaged in nonconsensual activity. I pray that you can see that by looking in my eyes."

item.title: Biden accuses Pelosi of working 'furiously' behind scenes to derail his 2024 campaign
item.description: Joe Biden's new book claims Nancy Pelosi worked behind the scenes to get his delegates to defect, though she has denied playing a role in any pressure campaign.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden wrote in his new book published Tuesday that former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi worked "furiously" behind the scenes to get elected officials and Biden delegates to abandon him in 2024, though Pelosi has denied leading a pressure campaign.

"That same morning, after an appearance on Morning Joe, Nancy Pelosi came to see me privately in the White House. She had been a great friend through the years. I admired her skill as Speaker and as a legislative leader. I always saw her as the political operator who learned the trade from her father, Tommy D'Alesandro, the former mayor of Baltimore, as opposed to the wealthy, liberal San Francisco Democrat caricatured in the Republican attack machine," Biden wrote.

Pelosi, in July 2024, following Biden's disastrous debate performance, said during an interview on "Morning Joe," "It’s up to the president to decide if he is going to run." The remarks suggested Biden was still weighing his options despite his insistence at the time that he would remain in the race.

HILLARY CLINTON HAMMERS JOE BIDEN FOR 2024 REELECTION BID DESPITE SUPPORTING CAMPAIGN: 'TERRIBLE MISTAKE'

"Now, she was making a 'strategic reassessment.' Publicly she was still saying it was my decision to make. But privately she was working furiously behind the scenes to get elected officials and Biden delegates to defect," the former president wrote of Pelosi.

Biden's book, "Promise Me, America," was published Tuesday and details his decision to exit the 2024 presidential race, as well as his reasons for seeking a second term, among other topics.

JOE BIDEN SAYS CANCER SLOWED HIM DOWN, LIMITING MEMOIR PROMOTION TOUR

The former president said Pelosi had heaped praise on him during their July 2024 meeting but sounded the alarm on the polling.

"Then she told me how terrible my polling was and that I would be dragging her most vulnerable members down. She told me all the polling she had seen said I couldn't win, but I could be the George Washington of our time if I passed the torch," he wrote.

EX-BIDEN STAFFER BLAMES BIDEN'S 'HUBRIS' FOR THE 'HELLSCAPE THAT WE LIVE IN': REPORT

Biden wrote that Pelosi asked him to call one of his senior advisors, Mike Donilon, to go over the polling.

"I told her I trusted Mike. That he had been with me for forty years. And he had been right in 2016 and 2020 and 2022 when so many of the pollsters had gotten it wrong. Mike walked her through the numbers, making the case that the race was close and still winnable. She didn't buy any of it. She told me that I wasn't getting an honest assessment of where the race stood. She was blunt: There were no polls that said I had any chance to win," Biden wrote.

JILL BIDEN ADMITS PRESIDENT BIDEN WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN ABLE TO SERVE ANOTHER FOUR YEARS

Biden ultimately dropped out of the race on July 21, 2024. He maintained in his book that he believed he was the best person to run against President Donald Trump, who defeated former Vice President Kamala Harris after she replaced Biden at the top of the Democratic ticket.

Pelosi denied leading a pressure campaign in interviews following Biden's decision.

JILL BIDEN REVEALS JOE WHISPERED 'I REALLY F---ED UP' AFTER DISASTROUS DEBATE WITH TRUMP

During a "60 Minutes" interview in August 2024, Lesley Stahl told Pelosi that it had been reported Biden was "furious" with her. 

"I understand that you don't want to own this. But it is so well-reported that you were the leader of a pressure campaign," Stahl said.

"No, I wasn't a leader of any pressure party. Well, let me say things that I didn't do. I didn't call one person. I did not call one person. I could always say to him, 'I never called anybody.' What I'm saying is, I had confidence that the president would make the proper choice for our country, whatever that would be, and I said that. 'Whatever that is, we'll go with,'" Pelosi responded.

During a December 2025 interview, USA Today's Susan Page asked Pelosi about the role she played in getting Biden to exit the race and whether she had spoken to him since.

JOE BIDEN ADDRESSES CRITICS WHO SAID HE HID HIS STAGE 4 CANCER DIAGNOSIS IN UPCOMING MEMOIR

"No, but I want to just recharacterize what you said. My conversations with the president were more about let's make sure we're understanding what the polls say, and there are certain attitudes that the public had, had they been taken into consideration. If they had sat down with more pollsters, it might have come to a place where we said, ‘This is it, the president should go,’ but they just decided that their polls were right and that was that. So I didn't go in there to say to the president, 'You shouldn't run.' I said, ‘We've got to compare polls because we have different numbers,'" Pelosi said at the time.

Pelosi's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Biden listed the many people he called after he announced his exit. The list included Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., former President Bill Clinton, Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and several other Democratic governors, senators and representatives, as well as union leaders.

Pelosi was notably absent from the list. However, the former president said there were many others he wished he could have called.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Near the end of Biden's book, he wrote that he reunited with Pelosi at an Italian restaurant in early 2026, noting that she had made clear where she stood on his re-election effort.

"While I had seen Nancy and her family briefly at a couple of previous events, our last real conversation had been the one in which she told me that it was my decision whether to continue my run for president, making it clear what her decision was. We didn’t discuss that episode. But we had been through too much together to allow a rift to go un-mended. And so we talked about life and family and politics and fell into the old rhythms of friendship. And I’m glad we did," he wrote.

An Illinois ethanol plant worker with a lengthy criminal past was federally indicted Tuesday after prosecutors said he emailed a threat claiming explosive devices had been placed at the facility where he worked.

A federal grand jury indicted Andrew M. Kozak on Tuesday on charges of threats regarding explosives and interstate communications of a threat.

LIVE EXPLOSIVE DEVICE FOUND NEAR HOMELAND SECURITY OFFICE IN CLEVELAND, FORCING MASS EVACUATIONS

The indictment does not accuse Kozak of physically planting the explosive device found at the facility.

Kozak returned to BioUrja for work Monday morning and was taken into custody when he arrived, NBC Chicago reported, citing federal sources. FBI agents also executed a search warrant at his Chillicothe home, according to the outlet.

Kozak has a criminal past that includes several burglary-related felony convictions across four Nebraska counties and two stints in state prison, records reviewed by Fox News Digital show.

Kozak's criminal history stretches back two decades.

Kozak was also convicted in two Polk County felony burglary cases. One court record identifies Osceola High School, while another shows Kozak was ordered to pay restitution to Osceola Public Schools.

item.title: Tiger Woods' return to competitive golf coming at Hero World Challenge makes all the sense in the world
item.description: Tiger Woods' return to golf at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas comes 866 days after his last competitive round at the 2024 Open Championship.
item.content:encoded:
Tiger Woods will be making his return to competitive golf next month at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas. When he puts his tee in the ground and hits his opening round tee shot on December 3, a total of 866 days will have passed since his last competitive round of golf at the 2024 Open Championship.

It will also mark Woods' first start since his March 2026 rollover car crash in Florida that resulted in a DUI-related arrest and a trip to an inpatient treatment facility overseas.

Woods announced on Tuesday that he, along with Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland, had officially been added to the limited-field event held at Albany, and this being the 15-time major champion's return to golf makes all the sense in the world for multiple reasons.

For starters, Woods is the host of the Hero World Challenge. Competing as a playing host not only makes sponsors and broadcast partners happy, but the event itself is among the most laid-back environments in all of professional sports.

Woods will be competing against some of the best players in the world, including World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler, who will be battling for a $5 million purse, but will enter the 20-person, no-cut event with zero expectations. The few hundred fans that make it on property and the thousands watching back home will simply relish in watching him make contact with a golf ball in a (somewhat) competitive setting.

Woods not finishing last among a field that includes 12 of the Top 25 players in the world would be a huge accomplishment. Completing 72 holes as pain-free as possible and putting together a few flash moments would also be considered a win for Woods and fans.

Woods, who turns 51 at the end of December, is now eligible to compete on the PGA Tour Champions circuit. Perhaps the Hero will serve as a test run before potentially teeing it up on the senior circuit when its season begins in late March. It will undoubtedly be a gauge as to where his game stands among the best players on Earth, and what he does after collecting those results will be fascinating to watch unfold.

Woods having his game in some sort of order and his health in check before taking a drive down Magnolia Lane at Augusta National in April is what both he and the golf world as a whole have been hoping to see during his lengthy stint away from the sport.
